pr_title: Support view buffer-based rendering in Blazor
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/49172.

Support larger HTML payloads by buffering and writing to the underlying `HttpResponseStreamWriter`, following a strategy similar to ViewBuffers in MVC. To avoid having to introduce new public API in the endpoints library and to avoid circular dependency chains between `M.A.Mvc.Razor` and `M.A.Components.Endpoints`, I opt-ed to copysource the relevant files from `M.A.ViewFeatures.Buffers` and make a few targeted modifications (relying on internal concrete implementations instead of public interfaces in method/constructor signatures), to make the code sharing a bit more sensible. In the future, we may consider moving the buffering logic to `M.A.Html.Abstractions` so that it can be used in both APIs, although the fact that `M.A.Mvc.Razor` has a transitive dependency on `M.A.Componnents.Endpoints` here.

issue_context.title: StaticHtmlRenderer uses synchronous writes which eventually fails
issue_context.body:
All the prerendering logic inside `StaticHtmlRenderer` (and wrapper logic in `EndpointHtmlRenderer`'s `WriteComponentHtml`) performs synchronous writes against a `TextWriter` that wraps the output stream. 

This works up to a point, but once you write too much content (presumably exceeding the writer's internal buffer), the system will throw *InvalidOperationException: Synchronous operations are disallowed. Call WriteAsync or set AllowSynchronousIO to true instead.*. This can happen with or without streaming SSR.

Likely solutions:

 * We may be able to change the prerendering logic to use asynchronous writes throughout
 * Or we may need to write the prerendering output to a buffer and then asynchronously flush that to the response writer at the end of each batch
comments:
@SteveSandersonMS I think we might need to buffer, similar to how MVC does it.

What's your gut feeling since you've been working in this area. Do you favor changing the logic to be async, or buffer the entire response like MVC does.

I'd at least look at changing the logic to be async, but my gut feeling is we would likely end up siding with the buffers.

The part about async that bothers me the most is that these are big methods with *so many* fine-grained write calls, I worry that the async state machines would be immense and perhaps there would be a lot of overhead from that.

Ultimately the ideal would be to try both and benchmark, but at this stage I would be fine with us just building on the experience we have from MVC and take a similar approach.

@SteveSandersonMS we might be able to minimize the async state machine overhead. We are not going to be doing concurrent writes, so it is very likely we can implement `IValueTaskSource` within the `EndpointHtmlRenderer` and avoid the allocations even when we go async.

> We may be able to change the prerendering logic to use asynchronous writes throughout

Just looking at the code here again, there's an important reason why it's currently synchronous. We need the render buffers not to be mutated during this process. Doing this asynchronously (at least, to do it properly) would require adding some new primitive to our sync context to make it go into a locked state where it queues up incoming work even if no thread is currently holding it. Otherwise, each time we yield, other renders could occur and we'd end up in a corrupted state.

There may also be other aspects of the HTML rendering process that are built around an assumption of synchrony, so that would also require careful analysis if we were going to change it.

The alternative of using MVC-like viewbuffers is a more well-trodden path so may be the safer option for .NET 8 given that this change has to go in a very late preview (RC1 I think).
